about: Allele-identity cases. Each pairs a database record of a variant with what a subject's data holds at that position, and says whether the data matches the record. 'no_match' means the data does not confirm the record, so a pipeline must not report it; it does not mean the person is free of the variant. Array genotypes are taken as written on the forward strand of the record's genome build. Coordinates, ids and letters are synthetic and do not describe any real variant or person.

cases.why: The record is a deletion-insertion (AA>C). An array reports two single letters, and A/C fits a plain A>C SNP as well as this record. Two letters cannot tell them apart, so the record must not be reported from this data. It is not ruled out either.

The record is a one-base deletion written with its anchor base, so its alternate allele is the single letter C. A person without the deletion also shows C here. A rule that looks for the alternate letter reports everyone.
The genotype holds G and C. The record's alternate allele is A, so the data shows a different variant at this position.
The data row's own alternate allele is A and the record's is T. Same position, different variant.

T is neither allele of the record. On the forward strand the genotype holds the record's G and a third allele; on the reverse strand it reads C/A and holds no G. The array alone cannot say which, so the record must not be reported, and it is not ruled out.
Both delete bases after the same anchor: one base in the record, two in the data row. Same position, different deletion.

The record and the data row give different reference bases at the same coordinates. Two correct records on one genome build cannot disagree about the reference, so one of them is on another build or coordinate system, or is simply wrong. Do not match, and flag the row.

After trimming, both look like the same one-base deletion. But the record's reference is CAA and the data row's is CAT: they disagree about the third base, which trimming throws away. A rule that compares only the trimmed alleles matches them.
An exact single-letter match: one copy of the record's alternate allele, the other copy reference.
Two copies of the record's alternate allele.
The data row's reference and alternate alleles equal the record's, and the genotype holds the alternate.
The same one-base deletion written with a longer anchor (CAA>CA instead of CA>C). Comparing the letters misses it; comparing minimal representations matches it.
